chapter_summary: Jesus describes himself as the door and the good shepherd who knows his sheep and lays down his life for them. At the Feast of Dedication, opponents challenge him, attempt to stone him, and try to arrest him; Jesus withdraws beyond the Jordan, where many believe.
main_lesson: Jesus knows and protects his sheep, freely lays down his life, and speaks of his unity with the Father. His words and works demand a response, even when opponents react violently.

memory_verse.kjv: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
memory_verse.little_bible: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.

parent_guide: Access: primarily ages 9–12 with adult guidance; selected shepherd passages may suit ages 6–8. Sensitivity: theft, killing, destruction, abandonment, predatory animals, accusations of demon possession and madness, attempted stoning and arrest, death and sacrifice, religious conflict, and complex claims about Jesus and the Father. Keep the door, shepherd, sheep, thief, wolf, flock, and hand language as metaphors rather than turning them into codes about particular modern people. The hostile group in this scene does not represent all Jewish people; Jesus, his disciples, and the first hearers are Jewish. Verses 28–29 express lasting divine protection but must not be used to promise physical safety or silence a child reporting harm. Verses 30–38 contain major claims about Jesus' unity with the Father and a disputed interpretation of Psalm 82; Christian traditions articulate these texts differently. Jesus' willing death is unique and must never be used to encourage children to accept abuse, seek danger, or sacrifice their safety.
application_for_children: Children can learn Jesus' words carefully, value trustworthy care, refuse unsafe secrecy or demands, tell a safe adult about danger, and ask honest questions about difficult claims. Following Jesus never requires following an unsafe adult or staying near someone who harms them.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.
verses.little_bible: Truly, truly, I tell you: anyone who does not enter the sheepfold by the door, but climbs in another way, is a thief and a robber.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Someone who climbs into the sheepfold instead of using the door is a thief and robber.
verses.meaning: Jesus begins a shepherding figure of speech contrasting rightful entry with intrusion; the identities within the image unfold in the following verses.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me recognize trustworthy care.
verses.discussion_question: What two ways of entering does Jesus contrast?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how safe caregivers respect boundaries; anyone may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Practise asking a trusted adult before opening a door or gate.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour of an ancient Judean sheepfold with a visible doorway and a distant shadow climbing elsewhere, non-frightening, no text.

verses.kjv: But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
verses.little_bible: But the one who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The shepherd enters through the door.
verses.meaning: The shepherd's proper entry contrasts with the intruder's approach.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach me about your shepherd care.
verses.discussion_question: Who enters by the door?
verses.family_discussion: Notice what makes the shepherd's entrance different.
verses.do_it_today: Draw or trace a safe path through a doorway.
verses.illustration_prompt: Gentle storybook watercolour of a shepherd entering an ancient sheepfold through its door, culturally accurate, no text.

verses.kjv: To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
verses.little_bible: The gatekeeper opens for him, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The gatekeeper opens. The shepherd calls his sheep by name and leads them out.
verses.meaning: The image stresses recognition, belonging, and the shepherd's personal leadership.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for knowing your people.
verses.discussion_question: What does the shepherd do for his own sheep?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about how trustworthy leaders guide without forcing unsafe obedience.
verses.do_it_today: Use someone's name kindly when greeting them.
verses.illustration_prompt: Warm storybook watercolour of a gatekeeper opening as a shepherd calls sheep from a stone fold, no text.

verses.kjv: And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.
verses.little_bible: When he has brought out his own sheep, he goes ahead of them, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The shepherd goes ahead, and his sheep follow the voice they know.
verses.meaning: Ancient shepherds commonly led from the front; the sheep's recognition supports the relational metaphor.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me learn your trustworthy words.
verses.discussion_question: Why do the sheep follow?
verses.family_discussion: Compare familiar, trustworthy guidance with pressure from an unsafe person.
verses.do_it_today: Read one saying of Jesus with a trusted adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of a shepherd walking ahead of a flock on a safe path, ancient Judea, no text.

verses.kjv: And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.
verses.little_bible: They will not follow a stranger, but will run away from him, because they do not know the voices of strangers.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The sheep run from a stranger whose voice they do not know.
verses.meaning: Within the figure, unfamiliar voices do not gain the sheep's trust; this is not a command to fear every unfamiliar person.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom around unfamiliar people.
verses.discussion_question: How do the sheep respond to the stranger?
verses.family_discussion: Review a family safety rule for unfamiliar adults without teaching that every stranger is bad.
verses.do_it_today: Name a safe adult you can contact if approached unexpectedly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Gentle storybook watercolour of sheep keeping distance from an unfamiliar figure while staying near their shepherd, no menace, no text.

verses.kjv: This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them.
verses.little_bible: Jesus spoke this figure of speech to them, but they did not understand what he was telling them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus gave them this picture, but they did not understand it.
verses.meaning: John identifies the shepherd scene as figurative language and records the hearers' lack of understanding.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me ask when I do not understand.
verses.discussion_question: Did the listeners understand Jesus' picture?
verses.family_discussion: Make room for questions without embarrassment.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one honest question about something unclear.
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of Jesus teaching attentive but puzzled listeners near a sheepfold, culturally accurate, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.
verses.little_bible: Then Jesus said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you: I am the door of the sheep.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, “I am the sheep's door.”
verses.meaning: Jesus now identifies himself within the metaphor as the sheep's door, emphasizing access and protection.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me trust who you say you are.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus call himself?
verses.family_discussion: Explore what a sheepfold door does while keeping the image metaphorical.
verses.do_it_today: Notice one doorway and remember Jesus' words.
verses.illustration_prompt: Symbolic storybook watercolour of Jesus beside the doorway of a peaceful sheepfold, reverent, no text.

verses.kjv: All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.
verses.little_bible: All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Those who came before were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen.
verses.meaning: In the immediate metaphor Jesus condemns illegitimate claimants, not every prophet or every person who lived earlier; interpreters differ on the precise referents.
verses.prayer: Jesus, guard your people from false leaders.
verses.discussion_question: Whom did the sheep refuse to hear?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why strong religious claims should be checked with safe, knowledgeable adults.
verses.do_it_today: Pause before trusting one unverified claim.
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of sheep remaining safely inside while distant intruders turn away, restrained and non-violent, no text.

verses.kjv: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.
verses.little_bible: I am the door. If anyone enters through me, that person will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the door. Whoever enters through him will be saved and find pasture.
verses.meaning: Jesus presents himself as the way into salvation and the security and provision pictured by free movement and pasture.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for salvation and care.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus say the person entering through him will find?
verses.family_discussion: Name the parts of the shepherd image without promising that believers avoid all physical harm.
verses.do_it_today: Offer food or care to someone in your household if it is safe.
verses.illustration_prompt: Bright storybook watercolour of sheep passing through a safe doorway toward green pasture, ancient landscape, no text.

verses.kjv: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
verses.little_bible: The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I have come so that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The thief steals, kills, and destroys. Jesus came to give abundant life.
verses.meaning: The sharp contrast sets destructive intrusion against the abundant life Jesus brings; abundant life is not a guarantee of wealth, ease, or freedom from suffering.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for the life you give.
verses.discussion_question: What contrast does Jesus make?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss abundant life without equating it with money, comfort, or constant happiness.
verses.do_it_today: Choose one safe action that supports life or wellbeing.
verses.illustration_prompt: Hopeful storybook watercolour contrasting a shadowed empty sheepfold edge with Jesus leading sheep into light and pasture, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
verses.little_bible: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the good shepherd who gives his life for the sheep.
verses.meaning: Jesus identifies himself as the good shepherd whose willing death serves his sheep; this unique sacrifice does not command a child to endure harm.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for giving your life.
verses.discussion_question: What does the good shepherd do for the sheep?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that Jesus' sacrifice is unique and never excuses abuse or unsafe self-sacrifice.
verses.do_it_today: Receive care from a safe person without feeling you must earn it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent storybook watercolour of Jesus as a caring shepherd standing protectively with sheep, no violence, no text.

verses.kjv: But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep.
verses.little_bible: But a hired worker, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and runs away; and the wolf catches them and scatters the sheep.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A hired worker runs from the wolf, leaving the sheep to be caught and scattered.
verses.meaning: The hired worker's abandonment under threat contrasts with the good shepherd's costly commitment; the wolf remains part of the metaphor.
verses.prayer: God, bring trustworthy care to people in danger.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when the wolf comes?
verses.family_discussion: Acknowledge fear and abandonment without graphic detail; children may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Review whom to contact if a caregiver leaves you unsafe.
verses.illustration_prompt: Non-graphic storybook watercolour of a distant wolf scattering sheep while a hired worker retreats, subdued tension, no injury, no text.

verses.kjv: The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
verses.little_bible: The hired worker runs away because he is hired and does not care for the sheep.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The hired worker runs because he does not care for the sheep.
verses.meaning: Jesus attributes the worker's flight to lack of committed care, continuing the contrast with the good shepherd.
verses.prayer: Jesus, shape caregivers who truly care.
verses.discussion_question: Why does the hired worker run?
verses.family_discussion: Name signs of dependable care and remind children they may report neglect.
verses.do_it_today: Thank a dependable caregiver, if you wish.
verses.illustration_prompt: Gentle storybook watercolour of sheep together as a hired worker disappears in the distance, non-frightening, no text.

verses.kjv: I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
verses.little_bible: I am the good shepherd. I know my sheep, and my sheep know me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the good shepherd. He and his sheep know each other.
verses.meaning: Jesus describes reciprocal knowledge between himself and those who belong to him.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for knowing your people.
verses.discussion_question: Who knows whom in this verse?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about being known with care rather than watched with threat.
verses.do_it_today: Listen carefully when someone safely shares about themselves.
verses.illustration_prompt: Warm storybook watercolour of Jesus as shepherd recognizing individual sheep, peaceful ancient pasture, no text.

verses.kjv: As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep.
verses.little_bible: Just as the Father knows me, I also know the Father, and I lay down my life for the sheep.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father and Jesus know each other, and Jesus lays down his life for the sheep.
verses.meaning: Jesus connects his knowledge of the sheep with the mutual knowledge of Father and Son and again announces his willing death.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for your willing love.
verses.discussion_question: What two relationships does Jesus describe?
verses.family_discussion: Keep Jesus' voluntary mission distinct from demands that vulnerable people accept harm.
verses.do_it_today: Choose a safe, ordinary act of care that costs some time.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent symbolic watercolour of Jesus the shepherd under warm heavenly light among sheep, no depiction of death, no text.

verses.kjv: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.
verses.little_bible: And I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them too, and they will hear my voice; and there will be one fold and one shepherd.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus will bring other sheep too. They will become one fold with one shepherd.
verses.meaning: Jesus speaks of gathering others beyond the present fold into one flock; Christians commonly connect this with the inclusion of Gentiles, though the verse itself does not name them.
verses.prayer: Jesus, gather your people in peace.
verses.discussion_question: What will happen to the other sheep?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss unity that welcomes people without erasing their cultures or demanding unsafe conformity.
verses.do_it_today: Include someone in a safe shared activity.
verses.illustration_prompt: Inclusive storybook watercolour of two groups of sheep joining around one shepherd, diverse landscape, no text.

verses.kjv: Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again.
verses.little_bible: For this reason my Father loves me: because I lay down my life so that I may take it up again.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father loves Jesus, who lays down his life and will take it up again.
verses.meaning: Jesus links his voluntary death and taking up life again with the Father's love; this belongs to his unique mission and anticipates resurrection.
verses.prayer: Father, thank you for Jesus' death and resurrection.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus say he will do after laying down his life?
verses.family_discussion: Hold death and resurrection together, without implying love must be earned by suffering.
verses.do_it_today: Create a two-part picture showing sorrow followed by hope.
verses.illustration_prompt: Symbolic storybook watercolour showing a shepherd's staff laid down beside dawn light, resurrection hope, no graphic imagery, no text.

verses.kjv: No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.
verses.little_bible: No one takes it from me, but I lay it down by my own choice. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. I received this command from my Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus freely lays down his life and can take it up again, as his Father commanded.
verses.meaning: Jesus stresses his authority and willing agency in death and resurrection while also acting under the Father's command.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for freely completing your mission.
verses.discussion_question: What authority does Jesus say he has?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that this verse never authorizes another person to control a child's body or safety.
verses.do_it_today: Practise saying, “My body needs safety,” with a trusted adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent symbolic watercolour of Jesus holding a shepherd's staff against sunrise, calm authority and hope, no text.

verses.kjv: There was a division therefore again among the Jews for these sayings.
verses.little_bible: Therefore there was division again among the Jews because of these words.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: These words divided the Jewish listeners again.
verses.meaning: Jesus' claims produce disagreement among the Jewish people present; this must not be generalized to all Jewish people.
verses.prayer: God, help us disagree without contempt.
verses.discussion_question: What caused the division?
verses.family_discussion: Practise describing disagreement without insulting a whole community.
verses.do_it_today: Use respectful words in one disagreement.
verses.illustration_prompt: Historically respectful storybook watercolour of Jewish listeners in two discussion groups around Jesus, no hostile caricature, no text.

verses.kjv: And many of them said, He hath a devil, and is mad; why hear ye him?
verses.little_bible: And many of them said, “He has a demon and is mad. Why do you listen to him?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many insulted Jesus, saying he had a demon and was mad.
verses.meaning: Some opponents dismiss Jesus with spiritual and mental accusations rather than engaging his words; the verse reports their claim without endorsing stigma.
verses.prayer: God, keep my words from mocking others.
verses.discussion_question: What accusation did some people make?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why mental-health or spiritual labels should not be used as insults.
verses.do_it_today: Replace one mocking label with respectful language.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour of some listeners speaking critically while Jesus stands composed, no frightening demon imagery, no text.

verses.kjv: Others said, These are not the words of him that hath a devil. Can a devil open the eyes of the blind?
verses.little_bible: Others said, “These are not the words of someone who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Others questioned the accusation because Jesus had opened blind eyes.
verses.meaning: Other listeners test the accusation against Jesus' speech and the healing narrated in chapter 9.
verses.prayer: God, help me examine claims fairly.
verses.discussion_question: What question did the others ask?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about checking accusations against evidence while respecting blind people.
verses.do_it_today: Ask, “What evidence supports that claim?”
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of thoughtful listeners questioning an accusation, with Jesus nearby, respectful and calm, no text.

verses.kjv: And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.
verses.little_bible: And it was winter during the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: It was winter at Jerusalem's Feast of Dedication.
verses.meaning: The scene shifts to the Jewish winter festival now called Hanukkah, commemorating the temple's rededication.
verses.prayer: God, thank you for the Jewish setting of Jesus' story.
verses.discussion_question: When and where does this scene happen?
verses.family_discussion: Learn respectfully about Hanukkah from a reliable Jewish source.
verses.do_it_today: Find Jerusalem on a map.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful winter storybook watercolour of ancient Jerusalem during the Feast of Dedication, Jewish setting, no text.

verses.kjv: And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon's porch.
verses.little_bible: And Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's Porch.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus walked in the temple's covered porch.
verses.meaning: Solomon's Porch was a covered colonnade in the temple complex, fitting the winter setting.
verses.prayer: Jesus, meet us as we learn your words.
verses.discussion_question: Where was Jesus walking?
verses.family_discussion: Look at an age-appropriate reconstruction of the temple complex.
verses.do_it_today: Notice a covered walkway or shelter.
verses.illustration_prompt: Historically grounded storybook watercolour of Jesus walking under Solomon's Porch in the Jerusalem temple complex, no text.

verses.kjv: Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly.
verses.little_bible: Then the Jews surrounded him and said, “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some Jewish people surrounded Jesus and asked him to say plainly whether he was the Christ.
verses.meaning: The group presses Jesus for an unambiguous messianic declaration; 'Christ' means Messiah, God's anointed king.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me bring honest questions.
verses.discussion_question: What did the group ask Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Distinguish a firm question from surrounding or intimidating someone.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one clear question without crowding the person.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour of a group gathered closely around Jesus beneath the temple colonnade, tense but non-violent, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you did not believe. The works I do in my Father's name testify about me.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said his works in the Father's name showed who he was, but they did not believe.
verses.meaning: Jesus points to his prior words and works as testimony to his identity and mission from the Father.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me consider your words and works.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus say testifies about him?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how actions can support a claim without treating every impressive act as proof from God.
verses.do_it_today: Compare one person's claim with their actions.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent storybook watercolour of Jesus answering listeners in Solomon's Porch, subtle scenes of compassionate works in the background, no text.

verses.kjv: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.
verses.little_bible: But you do not believe, because you are not among my sheep, as I told you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said they did not believe because they were not his sheep.
verses.meaning: Jesus applies the sheep metaphor to his opponents' unbelief; the verse describes this confrontation and must not become a label children use to exclude others.
verses.prayer: Jesus, keep me humble when others disagree.
verses.discussion_question: What reason does Jesus give for their unbelief?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why children should not decide who is beyond God's welcome.
verses.do_it_today: Avoid using an in-group label against someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: Symbolic storybook watercolour of Jesus teaching with sheep imagery faintly behind him, listeners thoughtful and divided, no text.

verses.kjv: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
verses.little_bible: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knows his sheep. They hear him and follow him.
verses.meaning: The shepherd metaphor joins hearing Jesus, being known by him, and following him; it does not make every inner impression Jesus' voice.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me learn and follow your teaching safely.
verses.discussion_question: What three things happen between Jesus and his sheep?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that claims of hearing Jesus should be tested and never override safety or Scripture.
verses.do_it_today: Read one recorded teaching of Jesus with a trusted person.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peaceful storybook watercolour of a shepherd calling sheep who follow along a clear path, no text.

verses.kjv: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
verses.little_bible: And I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus gives his sheep eternal life. No one can snatch them from his hand.
verses.meaning: Jesus promises eternal life and secure belonging to his sheep; Christian traditions differ over how this relates to perseverance, and it is not a promise against earthly injury or death.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for eternal life and secure belonging.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus give, and what can no one do?
verses.family_discussion: Separate eternal security from claims that believers cannot be physically harmed.
verses.do_it_today: Make an open-hand picture as a reminder of secure belonging.
verses.illustration_prompt: Gentle symbolic storybook watercolour of sheep safely gathered near an open protective hand motif, non-literal and reverent, no text.

verses.kjv: My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand.
verses.little_bible: My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of my Father's hand.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father gave the sheep to Jesus and is greater than all. No one can snatch them from the Father's hand.
verses.meaning: Jesus grounds the flock's security in the Father's supremacy and gift; an ancient textual variant affects the wording of what or who is 'greater than all.'
verses.prayer: Father, thank you for your strong care.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus say about his Father and the sheep?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss spiritual security while affirming practical safety plans and reporting harm.
verses.do_it_today: Review one way to reach a safe adult in an emergency.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent symbolic watercolour of a flock beneath warm protective light with an open hand motif, no text.

verses.kjv: I and my Father are one.
verses.little_bible: I and my Father are one.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus and his Father are one.
verses.meaning: Jesus makes a profound unity claim concerning himself and the Father. Trinitarian Christians understand unity of divine being without confusing the persons; other traditions interpret the wording differently.
verses.prayer: Father and Son, guide us into truth about who you are.
verses.discussion_question: What claim does Jesus make?
verses.family_discussion: Invite questions about this complex claim without pretending every detail is simple.
verses.do_it_today: Copy the verse exactly and mark any question you have.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent symbolic storybook watercolour of Jesus beneath unified warm light, avoiding literal portrayal of the Father, no text.

verses.kjv: Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
verses.little_bible: Then the Jews picked up stones again to stone him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The group picked up stones to kill Jesus.
verses.meaning: The opponents respond to Jesus' claim with an attempted execution by stoning; the verse describes a particular group, not all Jewish people.
verses.prayer: God, protect people facing violence.
verses.discussion_question: How did the group respond?
verses.family_discussion: Name the attempted violence without graphic detail; children may pause or pass.
verses.do_it_today: Review how to leave and seek help when conflict becomes threatening.
verses.illustration_prompt: Restrained storybook watercolour of tense opponents holding stones at their sides while Jesus stands at a safe distance, no impact or injury, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered them, Many good works have I shewed you from my Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works are you stoning me?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked which good work from his Father made them want to stone him.
verses.meaning: Jesus confronts the threatened violence by pointing to his many good works from the Father and asking for its stated basis.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help us oppose violence with truth.
verses.discussion_question: What question does Jesus ask?
verses.family_discussion: Do not treat Jesus' response as requiring a child to confront an armed person; leaving and getting help is wise.
verses.do_it_today: Practise moving toward safety instead of arguing during danger.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour of Jesus speaking calmly to a tense group with stones lowered, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.
verses.little_bible: The Jews answered him, “We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They said the issue was not his good work but what they considered blasphemy: a man making himself God.
verses.meaning: The opponents state that they perceive Jesus' claim as blasphemy, making himself God. John presents their charge as part of the conflict over Jesus' identity.
verses.prayer: God, help me seek truth without violence.
verses.discussion_question: What reason did they give for wanting to stone Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why religious disagreement never gives children permission to harm others.
verses.do_it_today: State a disagreement without a threat or insult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Historically respectful storybook watercolour of Jewish opponents answering Jesus in a tense temple setting, stones visible but unused, no caricature, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods?
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, You are gods’?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus quoted their law: “I said, You are gods.”
verses.meaning: Jesus quotes Psalm 82:6 and calls it part of their law. Interpretations differ over whether the psalm addresses human judges, rulers, Israel, or heavenly beings.
verses.prayer: God, give us care when reading difficult Scripture.
verses.discussion_question: What words does Jesus quote?
verses.family_discussion: Keep the quotation in context; it does not teach children that they are divine.
verses.do_it_today: Read Psalm 82 with a trusted adult if age-appropriate.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent storybook watercolour of Jesus teaching from a Scripture scroll before attentive listeners, no divine caricatures, no text.

verses.kjv: If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken;
verses.little_bible: If he called them gods, to whom God's word came—and Scripture cannot be broken—
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Scripture called those who received God's word “gods,” and Scripture cannot be broken.
verses.meaning: Jesus reasons from Scripture's wording and enduring authority; the sentence continues into verse 36, and the referent of 'them' follows the disputed Psalm 82 interpretation.
verses.prayer: God, help me handle Scripture faithfully.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus say cannot be broken?
verses.family_discussion: Notice that the argument continues into the next verse before drawing conclusions.
verses.do_it_today: Read verses 34–36 together rather than isolating one line.
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of an open Scripture scroll as Jesus continues teaching, attentive listeners, no text.

verses.kjv: Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?
verses.little_bible: Do you say of the one whom the Father set apart and sent into the world, 'You blaspheme,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked why they called it blasphemy when the one sent by the Father said, “I am God's Son.”
verses.meaning: Completing the argument, Jesus contrasts Scripture's use of 'gods' with the charge against the uniquely consecrated and sent Son of God.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach us what your title means.
verses.discussion_question: How does Jesus describe the one who said, “I am the Son of God”?
verses.family_discussion: Keep Jesus' unique sonship distinct from broader language about believers as God's children.
verses.do_it_today: Circle the actions attributed to the Father: set apart and sent.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent storybook watercolour of Jesus speaking beneath temple arches with warm light suggesting his sending by the Father, no text.

verses.kjv: If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.
verses.little_bible: If I do not do my Father's works, do not believe me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said not to believe him if he did not do his Father's works.
verses.meaning: Jesus invites his challengers to evaluate whether his works correspond to the Father's activity.
verses.prayer: God, help me examine claims truthfully.
verses.discussion_question: What condition does Jesus give?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss the difference between evidence and pressure to believe.
verses.do_it_today: Look for whether one claim and action match.
verses.illustration_prompt: Storybook watercolour of Jesus gesturing toward remembered acts of healing and mercy, respectful and non-sensational, no text.

verses.kjv: But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him.
verses.little_bible: But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I am in him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said his works could help them know that the Father was in him and he was in the Father.
verses.meaning: Jesus presents his works as evidence of the mutual indwelling of Father and Son, a central but complex claim interpreted within Christian teaching about their unity.
verses.prayer: Father and Son, lead us toward true understanding.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus want the works to help them know?
verses.family_discussion: Invite wonder and questions about mutual indwelling without using simplistic physical explanations.
verses.do_it_today: Write one question about the Father and Son for later study.
verses.illustration_prompt: Reverent symbolic watercolour of Jesus surrounded by warm interwoven light suggesting communion with the Father, no literal Father figure, no text.

verses.kjv: Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand,
verses.little_bible: Therefore they tried again to seize him, but he escaped from their hand.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They tried to arrest Jesus again, but he escaped.
verses.meaning: The opponents attempt to seize Jesus, but he gets away; the narrative preserves both the threat and his escape.
verses.prayer: God, guide people toward safety when threatened.
verses.discussion_question: What did they try to do, and what happened?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm that escaping danger is wise and does not show weak faith.
verses.do_it_today: Review a safe exit route with a trusted adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Non-graphic storybook watercolour of Jesus moving safely away through a temple colonnade as a group remains behind, no grabbing shown, no text.

verses.kjv: And went away again beyond Jordan into the place where John at first baptized; and there he abode.
verses.little_bible: And he went away again beyond the Jordan, to the place where John had first baptized, and he stayed there.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus crossed the Jordan and stayed where John had baptized before.
verses.meaning: Jesus withdraws across the Jordan to the setting of John's earlier ministry, reconnecting the narrative with John's witness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for places of rest after danger.
verses.discussion_question: Where did Jesus go and stay?
verses.family_discussion: Notice the movement from threat toward a quieter place.
verses.do_it_today: Identify a safe, calm place you may use when overwhelmed.
verses.illustration_prompt: Peaceful storybook watercolour of Jesus beside the Jordan River near a remembered baptism place, calm landscape, no text.

verses.kjv: And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle: but all things that John spake of this man were true.
verses.little_bible: And many came to him and said, “John did no miracle, but everything John said about this man was true.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many came to Jesus and said that everything John had said about him was true.
verses.meaning: People compare John's non-miraculous ministry with the truth of his testimony about Jesus; truthful witness is not measured only by spectacular signs.
verses.prayer: God, help me value truthful witness.
verses.discussion_question: What did the people say about John's words?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why a truthful person does not need to perform wonders to matter.
verses.do_it_today: Thank someone for one truthful, helpful word.
verses.illustration_prompt: Warm storybook watercolour of many people gathering around Jesus beside the Jordan and remembering John, no miracle spectacle, no text.

verses.kjv: And many believed on him there.
verses.little_bible: And many believed in him there.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many people there believed in Jesus.
verses.meaning: John closes the chapter by recording belief in Jesus at the place associated with John's testimony.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me respond honestly to the witness about you.
verses.discussion_question: How did many people respond?
verses.family_discussion: Allow belief questions without pressure, performance, or forced disclosure.
verses.do_it_today: Quietly reflect on one thing the chapter says about Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Hopeful storybook watercolour of a diverse crowd listening to Jesus beside the Jordan, peaceful and reverent, no text.
